title: Anatomy of Conjunctiva, Types of Conjunctivitis and Pterygium

questions.q: Conjunctiva is a transparent ___ membrane that does not cover the cornea.
questions.exp: Conjunctiva is transparent mucous membrane. It does not cover cornea. (Book p195)

questions.q: Match the part of conjunctiva with its location — 1) Bulbar  2) Forniceal  3) Palpebral … A) Lines inner surface of eyelids  B) Covers sclera  C) Fornix/junctional fold
questions.exp: Bulbar covers sclera; Forniceal is fornix fold; Palpebral lines inner surface of eyelids. (Book p195)

questions.q: Plica semilunaris and caruncle are described together as:
questions.exp: Plica semilunaris (represents nictitating membrane) and Caruncle (contains hair follicles) are bracketed as Rudimentary structures. (Book p195)

questions.q: Plica semilunaris represents the vestigial ___.
questions.exp: Plica semilunaris : Represents nictitating membrane (rudimentary). (Book p195)

questions.q: Caruncle is characterized by containing:
questions.exp: Caruncle : Contains hair follicles. (Book p195)

questions.q: The outermost layer of conjunctival histology is epithelium of which type? It contains Goblet cells, melanocytes and Langerhans cells.
questions.exp: Histology 1. Outermost layer : Epithelium (Non-keratinised stratified squamous). Contains Goblet cells, melanocytes, Langerhans cells. (Book p195)

questions.q: Goblet cells in the conjunctival epithelium secrete mucin forming the innermost layer of tear film on parasympathetic stimulation. A drug blocking this would affect:
questions.exp: Goblet cells : Secrete mucin (Forms innermost layer of tear film) on parasympathetic stimulation. (Book p195)

questions.q: The adenoid/lymphatic layer of conjunctiva develops after:
questions.exp: Adenoid/lymphatic layer : Develops after 3 months of age. (Book p195)

questions.q: The fibrous layer of conjunctiva contains ___ and blood vessels.
questions.exp: Fibrous layer : Contains nerve fibres & blood vessels. (Book p195)

questions.q: Conjunctiva is described as the only site of lymphatic drainage from the eye. Its drainage is:
opts: Medially to pre-auricular nodes, laterally to submandibular nodes
Medially to submandibular lymph nodes, laterally to peri-auricular & superficial parotid lymph nodes
Both sides to deep cervical nodes
questions.exp: Lymphatic drainage : Only site of lymphatic drainage from the eye. Medially -> Submandibular lymph nodes; Laterally -> Peri-auricular & superficial parotid lymph nodes. (Book p196)

questions.q: Conjunctivitis is also known as ___.
questions.exp: Conjunctivitis Aka Eye flu. (Book p196)

questions.q: Which is NOT listed among the symptoms of conjunctivitis on page 196?
questions.exp: Symptoms : Redness, Discharge sticking to eyelids, Foreign body sensation, Lacrimation, Itching (if allergic), Pain and loss of vision (LOV) : Corneal involvement. (Photophobia with halos is not listed). (Book p196)

questions.q: A patient with conjunctivitis reports itching as the chief complaint. The book indicates itching occurs in which type?
questions.exp: Itching (if allergic). (Book p196)

questions.q: In conjunctivitis, pain and loss of vision indicate:
questions.exp: Pain and loss of vision (LOV) : Corneal involvement. (Book p196)

questions.q: Circumcorneal redness (ciliary injection) is seen in all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Differential: Circumcorneal redness seen in -> Glaucoma, Uveitis, Corneal ulcer. Conjunctivitis shows conjunctival hyperemia. (Book p196)

questions.q: Photographs on page 196 compare conjunctival hyperemia vs circumcorneal hyperemia. Circumcorneal hyperemia is noted as seen in:
questions.exp: Note : Seen in : Glaucoma, uveitis, corneal ulcer (circumcorneal hyperemia). (Book p196)

questions.q: Subconjunctival hemorrhage is managed by:
opts: No treatment required, resolves spontaneously ≤2 weeks
questions.exp: Subconjunctival hemorrhage : No treatment required (Resolves spontaneously ≤2 weeks). (Book p197)

questions.q: Chemosis is defined as swelling of the ___.
questions.exp: Chemosis : Swelling of bulbar conjunctiva. (Book p197)

questions.q: Discharge in conjunctivitis is described as mucopurulent/watery and:
opts: Causes colored halos & stickiness which resolves on washing eye
questions.exp: Discharge : mucopurulent/watery. Causes colored halos & stickiness which resolves on washing eye. (Book p197)

questions.q: Match the inflammatory reaction with its pathology — 1) Papillae  2) Follicles … A) Lymphoid aggregates  B) Hypertrophied vessels
questions.exp: Papillae : Hypertrophied vessels. Follicles : Lymphoid aggregates. (Book p197)

questions.q: Using the etiology table on page 197, match discharge/reaction to cause — Mucopurulent + Papillary reaction / Mucopurulent + Follicular / Watery + Papillary / Watery + Follicular
questions.exp: Table: Discharge Mucopurulent + Papillary Bacterial; Mucopurulent + Follicular Chlamydia; Watery + Papillary Allergic; Watery + Follicular Viral. (Book p197)

questions.q: Acute mucopurulent conjunctivitis is most commonly caused by ___.
questions.exp: Acute mucopurulent conjunctivitis : m/c cause : Staphylococcus aureus. Treatment : Topical antibiotics. (Book p197)

questions.q: Acute purulent/hyperacute conjunctivitis/blennorrhoea — most common cause and route:
questions.exp: Acute purulent/hyperacute conjunctivitis/blennorrhoea : m/c cause : Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Route : Oculogenital. (Book p198)

questions.q: Clinical features of blennorrhea include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Clinical features : 1. Copious purulent discharge. 2. Swelling of eyelids -> Overhanging. 3. Intense pain. 4. Pre-auricular lymphadenopathy. (Book p198)

questions.q: Treatment for gonococcal blennorrhoea as per book:
opts: I.M. Ceftriaxone 1g single dose followed by Oral erythromycin x 2 weeks
questions.exp: Treatment : I.M. Ceftriaxone 1g single dose followed by Oral erythromycin x 2 weeks. (Book p198)

questions.q: Match membranous conjunctivitis with most common cause — 1) Membranous (overall/in adults)  2) Membranous in unimmunised children … A) Corynebacterium diphtheriae  B) Pneumococcus
questions.exp: Acute membranous conjunctivitis : m/c cause Overall/in adults : Pneumococcus. In unimmunised children : Corynebacterium diphtheriae. (Book p198)

questions.q: Membrane in membranous conjunctivitis is fused with epithelium and bleeds on removal, whereas pseudomembrane does not fuse and no bleeding on removal. Is this true?
opts: False – membranous does not bleed, pseudomembranous does
questions.exp: Acute membranous : membrane fused with epithelium -> Bleeds on removal. Acute pseudomembranous : membrane does not fuse -> No bleeding on removal. (Book p198)

questions.q: Angular/diplobacillary conjunctivitis — most common cause:
questions.exp: Angular/diplobacillary conjunctivitis : m/c cause : Moraxella lacunata/Axenfeld. (Book p198)

questions.q: In angular conjunctivitis, excoriation at canthi is more marked at ___ canthus.
questions.exp: Clinical features : Excoriation at canthi (Lateral > medial). Redness at intermarginal strip. Blepharitis. (Book p198)

questions.q: Treatment for angular conjunctivitis includes:
opts: Topical steroids only for 2 weeks (not effective for Moraxella lacunata)
Tetracycline 1% ointment ≥2 wks + Zinc boric drops (zinc blocks proteolysis)
Oral ceftriaxone single dose for gonococcal disease (not for angular type)
Surgical excision of conjunctiva with autograft (not indicated here)
questions.exp: Treatment : Tetracycline 1% eye ointment for ≥2 wks. Zinc boric eye drops. (Zinc blocks proteolytic activity). (Book p198)

questions.q: Match adenoviral conjunctivitis types with serovars — 1) Non-specific follicular 2) Epidemic keratoconjunctivitis (EKC) 3) Pharyngoconjunctival fever (PCF) … A) 8,19,37  B) 3,4,7  C) 1 to 11 & 19
questions.exp: Non-specific follicular : Serovars 1 to 11 & 19; EKC : 8,19,37; PCF : 3,4,7. PCF Associated with preauricular lymphadenopathy. (Book p199)

questions.q: Pharyngoconjunctival fever is associated with:
questions.exp: PCF : Associated with preauricular lymphadenopathy. (Book p199)

questions.q: Apollo conjunctivitis is also called ___.
questions.exp: Apollo conjunctivitis/Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis : Hemorrhage of palpebral & bulbar conjunctiva. (Book p199)

questions.q: Most common cause of acute hemorrhagic (Apollo) conjunctivitis is:
questions.exp: Causes : 1. Picornavirus : Enterovirus type 70, Coxsackie A24 (m/c). 2. Adenovirus type 11. (Book p199)

questions.q: A patient has a unilateral, painless nodule with umbilicated appearance at the lid margin that periodically sheds virus causing conjunctivitis. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum : Unilateral painless nodule with umbilicated appearance. Nodule contains viral particles. Periodic shedding -> Conjunctivitis. Treatment Surgical excision [if cosmetic indication (+)]. (Book p199)

questions.q: Match chlamydial types — 1) Adult inclusion 2) Trachoma 3) Ophthalmia neonatorum … A) A,B,Ba,C  B) D to K (+ other causes for neonatorum)
questions.exp: Adult inclusion D to K; Trachoma A,B,Ba,C; Ophthalmia neonatorum D to K (+ Other causes). (Book p199)

questions.q: Trachoma is also known as ___.
questions.exp: TRACHOMA Aka Egyptian ophthalmia. (Book p199)

questions.q: Route of transmission of trachoma — mnemonic 3F includes:
questions.exp: Route : mnemonic 3F – 1. Fingers 2. Flies 3. Fomites. (Book p199)

questions.q: Pathology of trachoma is which hypersensitivity reaction?
questions.exp: Pathology : Type IV hypersensitivity reaction : Active inflammation + cicatrization. Age group <10 yrs. (Book p200)

questions.q: Sago grain follicles in trachoma show Necrosis & ___ cells.
questions.exp: Sago grain follicles : Necrosis & leber. Necrosis & leber cells seen. m/c site Upper palpebral conjunctiva. (Book p200)

questions.q: Cicatricial signs in trachoma include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Cicatricial sign : Arlt's line (Line of cicatrization); Herbert's pits : Pathognomic D/t healing of limbal follicles; Pannus : Vascularisation of cornea superiorly. Horner Trantas is VKC. (Book p200)

questions.q: Arlt's line is shown in an image with markings Upper 1/3rd and Lower 2/3rd. It represents:
questions.exp: Arlt's line : Line of cicatrization. (Image shows lower 2/3rd vs upper 1/3rd). (Book p200)

questions.q: Pannus in trachoma is:
questions.exp: Pannus : Vascularisation of cornea superiorly. (Book p200)

questions.q: Complication sequence of untreated trachoma is:
opts: Trichiasis -> corneal ulcer -> scar -> loss of vision
questions.exp: Complications : Trichiasis (inturned eyelash) -> Corneal ulcer -> Scar formation -> Loss of vision. (Book p200)

questions.q: SAFE strategy for trachoma (WHO, 1996) includes all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: SAFE : Surgery for inturned eyelids, Antibiotics Azithromycin 1g, Facial cleanliness, Environmental change. (Book p200)

questions.q: For trachoma control, if prevalence in 1-9 yr old children is >10%, the management is:
questions.exp: Table: >10% Mass prophylaxis; 5-10% Treatment to affected children & family; <5% Facial cleanliness & environmental change advised. (Book p200)

questions.q: Match WHO FISTO classification — 1) TF  2) TI  3) TS  4) TT  5) CO … A) >5 follicles  B) Thickening of upper palpebral conjunctiva  C) Arlt's line  D) Eyelash growing inwards  E) Visual impairment
questions.exp: FISTO : TF >5 follicles + ; TI Thickening of upper palpebral conjunctiva; TS Arlt's line; TT Eyelash growing inwards; CO Visual impairment. TF/TI Active stage Antibiotics; TS Inactive No treatment; TT Requires surgery. (Book p201)

questions.q: Match onset after birth with cause of ophthalmia neonatorum — 1) Within first 6h  2) 24-48h  3) 2-5d  4) 5-7d  5) >1 wk … A) Neisseria gonorrhoeae (most severe)  B) Chemical (Silver nitrate)  C) Other bacteria  D) HSV-II  E) Chlamydia trachomatis D-K m/c
questions.exp: Onset table: Within 1st 6h Chemical (Silver nitrate); 24-48h Neisseria gonorrhoeae (most severe); 2-5d Other bacteria; 5-7d HSV-II; >1 wk Chlamydia trachomatis D-K m/c. (Book p201)

questions.q: Ophthalmia neonatorum is defined as conjunctivitis in neonates appearing within:
questions.exp: OPHTHALMIA NEONATORUM Conjunctivitis in neonates (<28 days of onset). (Book p201)

questions.q: Prevention of ophthalmia neonatorum — Crede's method with 1% Silver nitrate is:
questions.exp: Prevention : 1. Crede's method : Topical 1% Silver nitrate (Not recommended d/t chemical conjunctivitis). 2. 0.5% erythromycin or 3. 1% tetracycline Single application Within 1 hr of birth. (Book p202)

questions.q: Prophylaxis for ophthalmia neonatorum with erythromycin/tetracycline should be given:
opts: Within 1 hr of birth as single application
questions.exp: 0.5% erythromycin / 1% tetracycline Single application Within 1 hr of birth. (Book p202)

questions.q: Allergic conjunctivitis presents with the triad of:
questions.exp: Allergic conjunctivitis Presents with papillae reaction + watery discharge + itching. (Book p202)

questions.q: Vernal keratoconjunctivitis/Spring catarrh is which hypersensitivity? Eg pollen
questions.exp: VERNAL KERATOCONJUNCTIVITIS/SPRING CATARRH Type I hypersensitivity reaction (Eg : pollen). (Book p202)

questions.q: VKC incidence is age 5-15 yrs, males > females, young boys, most common in:
questions.exp: Incidence : Age 5-15 yrs, Males > Females (Young boys), m/c in spring & summer, H/O atopy present. (Book p202)

questions.q: In VKC, papillary hypertrophy shows cobble stone papillae with giant papillae > ___ size.
questions.exp: Papillary hypertrophy : Cobble stone papillae. Giant papillae : >1mm size. (Book p202)

questions.q: Horner Trantas sign in VKC is:
opts: Collection of eosinophils + epithelial debris on limbus
questions.exp: Horner Trantas sign : Collection of eosinophils + epithelial debris. Site : On limbus. (Book p202)

questions.q: Pseudogerontoxon described in VKC is:
opts: True arcus senilis in old age
Paralimbal grey-white band d/t lipid deposition in children, similar to arcus senilis
Iron line in front of pterygium
questions.exp: Pseudogerontoxon : Paralimbal grey-white band (D/t lipid deposition) in children. Appearance similar to arcus senilis. (Book p202)

questions.q: Which are additional features of VKC listed? Shield ulcer, Dennie Morgan line, Maxwell Lyon sign, pseudogerontoxon. Which association is given due to excessive itching?
questions.exp: Features: Shield ulcer (in cornea), Dennie Morgan line Extra lower-lid crease, Maxwell Lyon sign Ropy discharge, Note : Excessive itching -> increased incidence of Keratoconus. (Book p202)

questions.q: Treatment of VKC lists DOC as:
questions.exp: Treatment : 1. Cold compress 2. Topical anti-histamine 3. Topical mast cell stabilisers 4. DOC : Olopatadine or Alcaftadine 5. Topical steroids in acute exacerbation (For symptomatic treatment). (Book p203)

questions.q: Atopic keratoconjunctivitis is seen in:
questions.exp: ATOPIC KERATOCONJUNCTIVITIS seen in 2nd to 5th decade. (Book p203)

questions.q: Hertoghe sign in atopic keratoconjunctivitis is loss of ___.
questions.exp: Atopic Clinical : Eyelids : Hertoghe sign (Lateral eyebrow lost). Itching, Papillae, watery discharge. (Book p203)

questions.q: Giant papillary keratoconjunctivitis shows papillae >1mm, type IV hypersensitivity, mechanically induced by all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: GIANT PAPILLARY Etiology : mechanically induced by Contact lens, Ocular prostheses, Protruding sutures. (Book p203)

questions.q: Phlyctenular keratoconjunctivitis is type IV hypersensitivity to endogenous allergen. Most common cause in India is TB, in western countries is:
questions.exp: Etiology : m/c in India : TB. m/c in western countries : Staphylococcus aureus. (Book p203)

questions.q: A nodule near limbus grows towards cornea and ulcerates giving rise to sacrofulous, fascicular or miliary ulcer. This describes:
questions.exp: Phlycten : Nodule near limbus. Grows towards cornea -> Ulcerates. Gives rise to Sacrofulous ulcer, Fascicular ulcer, miliary ulcer. Treatment Topical Steroids. (Book p203)

questions.q: Pterygium is a triangular, fibrovascular growth of degenerative ___ tissue over cornea that destroys Bowman's layer & superficial stroma.
questions.exp: Pterygium Triangular, fibrovascular growth of degenerative sub-conjunctival tissue over Cornea. Destroys Bowman's layer & superficial stroma. (Book p204)

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as associated with pterygium?
questions.exp: Associated with UV ray exposure, Dust, Humidity. Cause Limbal stem cell deficiency -> Activation of matrix metalloproteinase. Site Nasal > Lateral. (Book p204)

questions.q: Stockers line in pterygium is:
opts: Iron deposition in front of apex
questions.exp: Clinical features : 2. Stocker's line : Deposition of iron in front of apex. (Book p204)

questions.q: Loss of vision in pterygium is due to:
opts: Both corneal astigmatism and encroaching into visual axis
questions.exp: Loss of vision. Causes : a. Corneal astigmatism. b. Encroaching into visual axis (Covers pupillary area). (Book p204)

questions.q: To reduce recurrence after surgical excision of pterygium, the book advises:
opts: Topical steroids alone for 1 month with lubrication only
Mitomycin C topically + Conjunctival autograft (same eye, superior) with sutures/glue/serum
Laser photocoagulation of conjunctival vessels alone
questions.exp: Treatment : Surgical excision : ↑ rate of recurrence. To reduce recurrence : 1. Topical mitomycin C. 2. Autograft : Harvested from same eye. Site : usually superior. Fixed with sutures/fibrin glue/autologous serum. (Book p204)

questions.q: Pinguecula is:
opts: Elastic degeneration of collagen in conjunctival stroma, common nasally
Benign neoplastic proliferation of conjunctival epithelium
Calcific degenerative plaque with calcium deposition
questions.exp: PINGUECULA Elastic degeneration of collagen fibres in stroma of conjunctiva. m/c site : Nasal part of conjunctiva. Image Yellowish fat-like nodules. (Book p205)

questions.q: Concretions are collection of epithelial debris & mucus caused by irritation due to friction of eyelid against bulbar conjunctiva & cornea while ___.
questions.exp: CONCRETIONS Collection of epithelial debris & mucus. Cause : Irritation d/t friction of eyelid against bulbar conjunctiva & cornea while blinking. (Book p205)

questions.q: Treatment and note about concretions:
opts: Surgical excision with no recurrence; contains calcium
Removal with 26g needle, spontaneously resolves with good lubrication; concretions do not contain calcium deposits
questions.exp: Treatment : Removal with 26g needle. Spontaneously resolves with good lubrication. Note : Concretions do not contain calcium deposits. Images minute yellowish-white elevations. (Book p205)
